title: Oakridge Outfitters: idle cash, securities and changes in equity
judge_role: Chief financial officer of OAKRIDGE OUTFITTERS, which has $500,000 of cash it will not need for 6 months

difficulty.rationale: Stock table, money vs capital markets and statement of changes in equity.

scenario:
You are to assume the role of staff accountant at OAKRIDGE OUTFITTERS, a retailer of camping and hiking gear. The chief financial officer (CFO) of OAKRIDGE OUTFITTERS (judge) has asked for your advice on investing extra cash and on presenting the company's equity for the year.

OAKRIDGE OUTFITTERS has $500,000 in its checking account that it will not need for 6 months. At that time, the full amount will be used to build and stock a new store. At a recent management meeting, the chief executive officer suggested buying shares of a well known outdoor equipment company whose products OAKRIDGE sells, "because everyone knows the brand." The CFO (judge) printed the stock's line from a financial website but is not sure how to read it.

[Stock table line: see exhibits]

The CFO (judge) is also preparing the year-end financial statements for the company's bank and needs a statement of changes in equity. The equity activity for the year is shown below.

[Equity activity this year: see exhibits]

The CFO (judge) wants to understand the choices available before making a recommendation to the chief executive officer.

You must:
- Describe the roles of different financial institutions
- Explain money markets and capital markets and recommend where to put the $500,000
- Describe sources of information about securities
- Interpret the stock table line
- Prepare the statement of changes in equity

You will present your recommendations to the CFO (judge) in a role-play to take place in the CFO's office. The CFO (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendations and have answered the CFO's (judge's) questions, the CFO (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
tasks: Describe the roles of different financial institutions
Explain money markets and capital markets and recommend where to put the $500,000

Prepare the statement of changes in equity

exhibits.title: Equity activity this year
rows: Issued 1,000 new shares of common stock (record the full amount in Common Stock)
Repurchased shares of its own stock (treasury stock)

judge_questions: Dividends are 3%, better than a savings account. Why not buy the stock?
Why does buying back our own shares reduce equity?

solution.overview: A strong answer describes the main financial institutions, explains that a 6-month need calls for the money market (Treasury bills, money market funds or CDs) rather than a stock that swung between $31.50 and $48.20, and names reliable sources of securities information. The presenter reads every column of the stock table (yield 3.0%, EPS about $2.67, previous close $39.25) and prepares a statement of changes in equity that grows from $550,000 to $670,000.

answer: Commercial banks accept deposits, make loans and offer business checking accounts and CDs
Credit unions are member owned and offer similar services, often with lower fees
Brokerage firms buy and sell stocks, bonds and money market funds for investors
Insurance companies protect against losses and invest the premiums they collect
Investment banks help companies raise money by issuing stocks and bonds, for example in an IPO
Money market: short-term (one year or less), low risk and very liquid, such as Treasury bills, money market funds and CDs
Capital market: long-term stocks and bonds with higher expected returns and higher risk
The cash is needed in 6 months, so safety and liquidity matter most
Recommend Treasury bills, a money market fund or a 6-month CD, not stock
OUTD traded between $31.50 and $48.20 this year, about a 35% drop from high to low, so $500,000 could lose much of its value right when the store needs it
SEC EDGAR filings, such as the 10-K (annual report) and 10-Q (quarterly report)
The company's investor relations website: earnings releases and presentations
Brokerage platforms and their research reports
Financial news and market data services, including stock tables
52-week high and low: the price ranged from $31.50 to $48.20 over the past year
Dividend $1.20 per share per year; yield = 1.20 / 40.00 = 3.0%
P/E of 15: the price is 15 times earnings per share, so EPS = 40 / 15 = about $2.67
Last $40.00 is the closing price; net change +$0.75 means the previous close was $39.25
Retained earnings: 350,000 + 120,000 minus 40,000 = $430,000
Treasury stock: ($10,000), shown as a subtraction from equity
Total equity rises from $550,000 to $670,000

calculations.label: Statement of changes in equity
steps: Retained earnings: 350,000 + 120,000 net income minus 40,000 dividends = $430,000

judge_question_answers.question: Dividends are 3%, better than a savings account. Why not buy the stock?
answer: A 3% dividend on $500,000 is only about $15,000 a year, or about $7,500 for 6 months
A 10% drop in the price would lose $50,000, far more than the dividend
Dividends are not guaranteed and can be cut
Money market choices pay less but protect the $500,000 the new store needs

judge_question_answers.question: Why does buying back our own shares reduce equity?
answer: When the company buys back shares, cash leaves the business and goes to the selling shareholders
Assets go down, so the owners' claim on those assets (equity) goes down too
Treasury stock is a contra equity account shown as a subtraction, not an asset
No gain or loss is recorded; if the shares are later resold, equity goes back up

key_concepts.definition: A business that handles money for others, such as a commercial bank, credit union, brokerage firm, insurance company or investment bank.
The market for short-term (one year or less), low-risk, highly liquid investments such as Treasury bills, money market funds and CDs.
The market for long-term securities such as stocks and bonds, with higher expected returns and higher risk.
How quickly an asset can be turned into cash without losing value.
A short-term U.S. government debt security that is very safe and easy to sell.
A summary of a stock's trading data, including its 52-week high and low, dividend, yield, P/E ratio, last price and net change.
Annual dividend per share divided by the stock price.
Stock price divided by earnings per share; it shows how much investors pay for each dollar of earnings.
The SEC's free online database of public company filings, including the 10-K and 10-Q.
A financial statement that shows how each part of owners' equity changed during the period.
Total profits kept in the business. Ending = beginning + net income minus dividends.
A company's own shares that it has bought back. It is subtracted from equity and is not an asset.

notes: State level because the student must connect a 6-month time horizon to the right market, read every column of a stock table and build a simple equity statement. Watch for students who recommend the stock because of its dividend, who treat treasury stock as an asset, or who forget to subtract dividends from retained earnings.

items.label: Describe the role of financial institutions

criteria.exceeds: Describes commercial banks (deposits, loans, CDs), credit unions (member owned, often lower fees), brokerage firms (buy and sell stocks, bonds and money market funds), insurance companies and investment banks (help companies issue stocks and bonds, such as an IPO), and links each to where OAKRIDGE could place or access its $500,000.
criteria.meets: Correctly describes at least three types of financial institutions and what each does for a business like OAKRIDGE OUTFITTERS.
criteria.below: Names institutions but describes their roles vaguely or mixes them up, for example saying banks sell stocks.
criteria.little: Does not describe any financial institutions or their roles.

criteria.exceeds: Contrasts the money market (one year or less, low risk, very liquid) with the capital market (long-term stocks and bonds, higher return and risk), recommends Treasury bills, a money market fund or a 6-month CD because the cash is needed in 6 months, and shows that OUTD swung from $48.20 to $31.50, about a 35% drop, which could wipe out much of the store money.
criteria.meets: Explains the difference between money and capital markets and recommends a money market choice rather than the stock because the cash is needed in 6 months.
criteria.below: Defines the markets vaguely, or recommends a mix that still puts much of the $500,000 in stock without addressing the 6-month need.
criteria.little: Does not explain the markets, or recommends buying the stock because the brand is well known or the dividend is 3%.

criteria.exceeds: Names SEC EDGAR filings such as the 10-K and 10-Q, the company's investor relations website, brokerage platforms and research reports, and financial news and market data services, and explains what the CFO would learn from each instead of relying on brand familiarity.
criteria.meets: Identifies at least three reliable sources, including SEC filings, company investor relations and financial news or brokerage research.
criteria.below: Names only one or two general sources, such as the internet or the news, without explaining their value.
criteria.little: Does not identify any sources of securities information.

criteria.exceeds: Reads every column: 52-week range $31.50 to $48.20, dividend $1.20 per share, yield 1.20 / 40.00 = 3.0%, P/E 15 so EPS is about $2.67 (40 / 15), last price $40.00 and net change +$0.75 so the previous close was $39.25, and explains what each means for the investment decision.
criteria.meets: Correctly explains most columns, including the 52-week range, the 3.0% yield, the P/E of 15 and the $40.00 closing price with a $0.75 gain.
criteria.below: Explains only a few columns, or misreads one, such as treating the $1.20 dividend as the yield or the P/E as a percentage.
criteria.little: Cannot interpret the stock table line.

items.label: Explain the nature of statements of changes in equity

criteria.exceeds: Prepares the statement with Common Stock rising from $200,000 to $250,000, Retained Earnings from $350,000 to $430,000 (plus $120,000 net income, minus $40,000 dividends) and Treasury Stock of ($10,000), total equity rising from $550,000 to $670,000, and checks the total, explaining why the bank wants to see these changes.
criteria.meets: Prepares the statement correctly, reaching ending total equity of $670,000 from beginning equity of $550,000.
criteria.below: Makes an error such as forgetting to subtract the $40,000 dividends, adding treasury stock instead of subtracting it, or leaving out the $50,000 share issue.
criteria.little: Does not prepare the statement, or the amounts are unrelated to the equity activity.

items.label: Critical Thinking: Reason effectively and use systems thinking

criteria.exceeds: Connects the 6-month time horizon, the stock's 35% swing and the new store's cash need to the choice of market, and explains how dividends, share issues and buybacks each change equity.
criteria.meets: Reasons correctly from the time horizon to a safe, liquid investment and from the equity activity to the statement.
criteria.below: Reaches conclusions without showing the reasoning, or misses the link between risk and timing.

items.label: Problem Solving: Make judgments and decisions and solve problems

criteria.exceeds: Gives the CFO a clear recommendation (Treasury bills, a money market fund or a 6-month CD, not OUTD stock) and a respectful way to explain it to the chief executive officer.
criteria.meets: Makes a clear recommendation to use the money market for the $500,000.
criteria.below: Hesitates, or gives a recommendation that is partly correct or not clearly stated.
criteria.little: Makes no recommendation, or recommends the stock.

criteria.exceeds: Explains the markets, stock table and equity statement in plain language the CFO can pass on to the chief executive officer, in a logical order, with confident and professional delivery.
criteria.meets: Presents all five topics clearly and in an organized way.
criteria.below: Presentation is hard to follow, relies on jargon, or skips topics.

items.label: Creativity and Innovation: Show evidence of creativity

criteria.exceeds: Uses a clear visual such as a labeled stock table, a risk comparison of the choices, or a neat equity statement layout, and adds a useful idea such as matching the CD or T-bill term to the store's opening date.
criteria.meets: Organizes the information in a way that makes the recommendation easy to understand.
criteria.below: Presents the facts with little effort to make them engaging or easy to follow.
criteria.little: Shows no evidence of creativity or original thought.

items.label: Overall impression and responses to the judge's questions

criteria.exceeds: Answers both questions correctly and confidently: a 3% dividend on $500,000 is only about $15,000 a year (about $7,500 for 6 months) while a 10% price drop would lose $50,000, and dividends can be cut; and a buyback sends cash out to shareholders, so assets and equity fall, with treasury stock shown as a contra equity subtraction, not an asset, and no gain or loss recorded.
criteria.meets: Answers both questions mostly correctly, including that the price risk outweighs the dividend and that treasury stock reduces equity because cash leaves the company.
criteria.below: Answers only one question correctly, or gives vague answers without numbers.
criteria.little: Cannot answer the judge's questions, or gives incorrect answers such as calling treasury stock an asset.

key_points: The $500,000 is needed in 6 months, so it belongs in the money market (Treasury bills, a money market fund or a 6-month CD), not the capital market
OUTD ranged from $31.50 to $48.20 over 52 weeks, about a 35% drop from high to low
Stock table: yield 1.20 / 40.00 = 3.0%; EPS = 40 / 15 = about $2.67; previous close 40.00 minus 0.75 = $39.25
Reliable sources: SEC EDGAR filings (10-K and 10-Q), company investor relations, brokerage research and financial news
A 3% dividend on $500,000 is about $15,000 a year, while a 10% price drop would lose $50,000
